stvoyHM.exe.IN_JoyMove: 0x43f3a0; axes X, Y, Z, R up to wNumAxes; v = (pos - 32768) * (1/32768) held to [-1, 1]; joy_xbutton read 0x43f66f (X), joy_ybutton 0x43f6d1 (Y); when 0, Sys_QueEvent(SE_JOYSTICK_AXIS, axis 0/1, ftol(-(v*127))) every frame at 0x43f6a0/0x43f715 (ftol 0x4a8570 truncates), 0 for -joy_threshold <= v <= joy_threshold; when 1, Quake III direction bits for v < -joy_threshold and v > joy_threshold; Z and R always direction bits
stvoyHM.exe.CL_JoystickMove: 0x409f10; anglespeed = 0.001 * frametime (* cl_anglespeedkey with +speed); yaw += cl_yawspeed * 0.01f (0x4b7430, 0x3c23d70a, 0x409f64) * axis[0] * anglespeed unless +strafe, else rightmove = ClampChar(rightmove + axis[0]); pitch += cl_pitchspeed * 0.01f (0x409faa) * axis[1] * anglespeed with +mlook, else forwardmove = ClampChar(forwardmove + axis[1]); upmove = ClampChar(upmove + axis[2])

stvoy.exe.IN_JoyMove: JoyToF 0x42d880 (same normalisation and clamp); joy_xbutton read 0x42da67, joy_ybutton 0x42dad5; axis events at 0x42dac3 and 0x42db40 with ftol 0x46db60 (truncates); same threshold and direction-bit rule as Holomatch
stvoy.exe.CL_JoystickMove: 0x405640; the same as Holomatch's, with its own 0.01f at 0x47e4a8 (0x405694 yaw, 0x4056da pitch)
